title: Notice of Appeal
corrections: The respondent's service line -- 'TO: Respondent ______________________' -- had no field at all, and every gate passed on it: the builder dropped the rule as a signature line and check_unfilled_blanks then excused the loss by re-running the same detector, which is guide 9.14b's blind spot exactly. The cause is that SK_ROLE_CAPTION had no bare-rule gate while SK_OFFICE_CAPTION always had one, so 'REGISTRAR' -- printed two lines below as the first line of the court's mailing address, 'TO: REGISTRAR / COURT OF APPEAL FOR SASKATCHEWAN / 2425 VICTORIA AVENUE' -- claimed the rule belonging to the other addressee. A bare office is not only a signature caption; it is also how a form addresses something, and what separates the two is that a signature caption sits under a bare rule while an addressee sits under somebody else's answer.

title: Emergency Intervention Order
corrections: The printed option squares on this page had no checkbox. Form A sets its options as the letter 'G' in WPTypographicSymbols, WordPerfect's symbol face, where G is the open square -- so the codepoint is U+0047 and carries no signal at all, and the builder's BOX_GLYPHS could not hold it without turning every G in the body text into a control. The discriminator has to be the font, the same way Manitoba's '[ ]' had to be cut by width rather than by codepoint (guide 9.13). All 28 marks across the eight pages were affected; the form now carries 28 checkboxes of a uniform 6.0x6.0, each seated on its own printed square.
notes: Six provisions options plus the tail and continuation writing lines of each; the victim, respondent and address lines and the judicial-centre blank all present.

title: Certificate of Compliance with Practice Directive 7
corrections: The 'E-mail address (if any)' field was 18pt short at the left, leaving a stub of printed writing line beside it and stepping it out of its own column: five fields in that block start at x 288 and this one started at 306. The line carries two anchors -- the government draws the rule from 288 like its five siblings and also types a run of underscores over it from 306 -- and the typed run won. Fixed by taking the whole line where a drawn rule and a typed run share a right edge; that condition holds on exactly this one line in all 121 templates, which is what keeps the table borders that also run under inline blanks (Form 15-47 p9, p13) from dragging their boxes across the page.

title: Application for Information to Establish or Vary Support (FOAEAA)
corrections: The two options under item 4 shared one control: 'to establish a support provision' and 'to vary an existing support provision' are stacked 14.6pt apart inside a 25.3pt character cell, so each glyph's box contains most of the other's square, and raw ink returned one 8.0x16.6 box covering both -- leaving the first option with nothing to tick (guide 2, 'one mark is one candidate, never union the marks in range'). A further nine marks on this form and two on PD8_D were oversized the same way. Fixed by reading contiguous runs of ink rows inside the character box and keeping the square one: the intruder is never contiguous with the mark (2.4pt / 7.75pt / 1.9pt inside one cell). Masking the neighbouring characters -- Manitoba's fix for the same class, guide 9.13 -- was tried first and is wrong here, because the cells overlap by more than half so the mask deletes the ink being measured and returned these marks 5.7 and 6.0pt tall.
